To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
All Right? has been effective in increasing the mental health wellbeing of tangata whaioratangata whaiora, including mental health clients, in Canterbury.
All Right? has had a positive impact for tangata whaiaora/mental health services users in Canterbury.

All Right? is having a positive impact on mental health service users, with the key facilitators being the campaign's focus on wellbeing, the use of humour, and the reduction of mental illness related stigma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how a population wide wellbeing campaign can be used to promote mental wellbeing and reduce stigma.
understanding how a population level campaign can impact tangata whai ora.
understanding the role of the community in the recovery process and how this role is facilitated by the community development work of mental health services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
All Right? was a positive wellbeing campaign for mental health service users in the Canterbury context.
All Right? has reached and positively impacted the wellbeing of mental health service users, and that this impact has been facilitated by the population wide nature of the campaign.
mental health service use is a risk factor for poor mental health outcomes in the post disaster environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the All Right? mental health service user evaluation demonstrated that All Right? had a positive impact on mental health service users, including increased wellbeing and decreased mental illness stigma, and that this impact was similar to, and in some cases greater than, the overall impact of All Right?.
mental health service use was not a barrier to engagement and that All Right? was a positive experience for tangata whairora.
All Right? is having an impact on tangata whai ora, and is helping to build a sense of community and connection in the post-earthquake environment in Canterbury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the All Right? message was well received and positively responded to by the mental health service user group.
wellbeing is a shared experience. It is not just about the individual, but also about their connections with others in their community.
